title: DR1 asks whether the consignment contains unweaned animals only when it holds cattle or pigs; the frontend also asks it for a horse-only consignment.

finding.frontend: The unweaned question is rendered when the notification's scope holds containsUnweanedAnimals (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/additional-details/template.njk:26-39), and the obligation puts it in scope when any commodity line's commodity is on an allow-list (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/aggregates.js:46-55). That allow-list is Cow and Horse, the only two of the frontend's five commodities on it. So a user importing horses alone is asked whether the consignment contains unweaned animals, and must answer before continuing.
finding.prototype: DR1 renders the question only when at least one selected commodity carries unweaned options, and only cattle and pig carry them — horse does not (app/data/commodities.js:11-60). DR1 additionally suppresses the question outright when every selected commodity is 01061900, which covers cat, dog and ferret. So on DR1 a horse-only consignment reaches this page, is asked what the animals are certified for, and is not asked the unweaned question at all.
finding.difference: Narrow the unweaned obligation so horses no longer trigger it, leaving cattle as the only frontend commodity that does; pigs would join it if the wider catalogue lands (commodities--commodity-catalogue). Before making the change, settle the contradiction: the frontend's obligation names its source as the V4 data fields and lists equines, cattle, pigs, sheep and goats, while DR1 records unweaned options against cattle and pig alone. One of the two is out of date and the designer has to say which.
finding.falsifiedBy: Opening DR1's additional-details page with only a horse species selected and finding the unweaned question rendered. Neither side was captured in that state — both captures are cattle consignments, where both sides ask the question — so this rests on the two rule definitions rather than on the pictures.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs and both full-page screenshots first: both captures are cattle consignments, both sides render the unweaned question with the same legend, the same hint and the same Yes/No, exactly as the finding says. Then traced both rules, because that is where the claim actually lives. DR1: app/routes.js:1158-1183 returns an empty option list unless a selected commodity carries unweaned options, only cattle and pig carry them, and app/routes.js:1187-1197 turns the question off when that list is empty — so a horse-only consignment is not asked. Frontend: the obligation puts the field in scope for any line whose commodity is on the unweaned allow-list, and that list is Cow and Horse in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:117, with the template rendering from that scope. Both cited ranges resolve exactly, including template.njk:26-39 and aggregates.js:46-55. Confidence "medium" is honest — the horse-only state is unphotographed on both sides and the falsifier says so plainly. CORRECT.
finding.correction: One understatement, left in the slot because it changes nothing: "DR1 additionally suppresses the question outright when every selected commodity is 01061900, which covers cat, dog and ferret" — that code also covers Other live mammals, so the suppression reaches four commodities rather than three. None of the four carries unweaned options in the first place, so the branch is belt and braces either way. Separately, the closing ask that the designer settle whether the V4 list or DR1 is out of date reads as a gate and is not one on this run: DR1 is the signed-off definition, which is why the band stays frontend-work. The question is still worth putting, because the contradiction only becomes live for sheep and goats once the wider catalogue lands.
